versions.summary: OpenCode transcript fixes and a session-locked model picker.
notes: Fixed OpenCode reasoning leaking into the chat: pre-role reasoning, late-arriving text after a tool call (which could append a duplicate), and inline <think> tags from some free models now render as proper thinking blocks instead of prose.

The model picker now locks to a started session's provider, greying out cross-provider rows. Switching mid-session to a stricter provider could replay the tool history to a new endpoint and hard-fail the turn.

versions.summary: Ollama harness, auto-named agent tabs, and a dedicated workstream GIT panel.
notes: Run your agents on local or remote Ollama models. Settings → Harnesses → Ollama probes any reachable server for its installed models and exposes them in the composer picker.

New agent tabs now auto-title from a summary of your first prompt with a small model (configurable in Settings → General). The title types out in the tab strip and locks once set — a manual rename is never overwritten.

A new GIT panel in the changes sidebar collects per-workstream git controls: an ahead/behind chip, base-branch retargeting that re-points an already-open PR, pull-base (fetch + merge), and a prune-fetch refresh. Archiving a merged workstream can now also delete its remote branch when you've opted in.

versions.summary: Scrollable tabs and OpenCode stability fixes.
notes: The tab strip is now scrollable: when tabs overflow, edge chevrons appear so you can scroll left and right without losing any open session.
Fixed live OpenCode model switching, auth token refresh, and Claude session resume and permission-mode handling so backend state stays consistent across reconfigurations.

versions.summary: OpenCode as an alternative agent backend, plus a re-runnable Commit action and a background-task fix.
notes: Run your agents on OpenCode as an alternative to the Claude CLI. A new Settings → Harnesses section configures each backend — model and provider pickers with per-provider API keys — and the session composer gains a harness and model picker. OpenCode Zen's free models work without a key.
The header Commit action now re-runs: clicking it again after making more changes sends a follow-up /commit turn to the still-live commit tab, instead of just re-selecting it.
Fixed phantom background tasks that could linger as “running” forever after the owning process died on an app restart, resume, rewind, or session exit.

versions.summary: A redesigned sidebar nav rail and unified Library, plus light-theme polish and session-recovery fixes.
notes: The left sidebar is rebuilt around a fixed activity-bar nav rail that stays visible at all times — Home, Projects, and Library up top, with Archive, Settings, and the update pill at the foot. The Projects button now toggles the project panel VS Code-style, the project panel and the diff sidebar glide open and closed instead of snapping, and project and workstream rows are restyled with an accent spine on the active row, larger repo avatars, and an even column of status dots.

The Library is now a single master–detail view: a resizable, collapsible doc list beside an inline detail pane, so opening a document keeps your list scroll and filters instead of swapping pages. It adds a project switcher, an inline filter box, type tabs, docs grouped by type, a per-field-editable frontmatter card, a Narrow/Wide width toggle, and a “View on GitHub” link for the open doc. Switching documents now always seeds a fresh editor buffer, fixing a case where one doc's unsaved edits could be saved over another.

Light theme: the pipeline-stage badges, doc-type chips, diff add/delete colors, knowledge-graph nodes, and live-activity dots now deepen to legible tints on the cream surface instead of washing out, while the dark themes are left visually unchanged.

Question prompts now offer a custom “Other…” free-text answer when none of the preset options fit — for a single-select question the typed text and a preset pick are mutually exclusive, for multi-select the text is appended after the picked options, and pressing Enter advances or submits.

Fixed sessions that could wedge forever as “working” when you hit Stop or changed the permission mode while the agent was parked on a permission prompt or question. Stop now declines the prompt and settles the session to idle, and changing the permission level clears the card, restarts into the new mode, and flushes any queued messages.

Fixed the undersized, blurry Windows app icon by regenerating it with a full set of resolutions (16–256px) from a dedicated full-bleed source, so the taskbar, Alt-Tab, Start menu, and large-icon shell views all render sharp.

versions.summary: Start workstreams from existing branches or in-place, pin worktrees, attach PRs, and Escape-to-close.
notes: New workstreams can now start three ways: an isolated new branch in its own worktree (the default), an existing local branch checked out into its own worktree, or in-place — switching the project's own checkout onto a branch with no separate worktree. The New Workstream dialog replaces the base-branch dropdown with a searchable branch picker, and in-place rows carry a “no worktree” badge in the sidebar and board. Archive, restore, and delete never move, re-link, or remove a branch or repo the app didn't create.

Attach a specific open PR to a workstream by number, overriding branch-name detection for status, preview, and merge — handy when a workstream's branch doesn't match its pull request. The new picker offers free-text search and a live preview of the number you enter.

Pin frequently used worktrees to a new “Pinned” section at the top of the project sidebar so they're reachable without expanding their project tree. Pin or unpin from a worktree row's context menu; pins persist per user and drop out automatically when a worktree is archived or deleted.

Press Escape to close the topmost open surface — a dialog, context menu, or the Settings page — through one shared handler stack, so a modal opened over a page closes first and the next Escape falls through to the page beneath. Escape still reaches the terminal or editor when nothing dismissible is open.

⌘W can no longer close the last window on macOS. The Close Window menu item — one key away from ⌘⇧W (Close Agent Tab) — has been removed, so a slipped shortcut can't shut the window out from under running sessions; ⌘Q and the red traffic-light button remain the deliberate exits.
The Ship / PR / Archive controls now stay pinned to the window's right edge and no longer shift when a diff sidebar opens.

versions.summary: An animated brand mark beside the working timer, plus terminal-toggle and repo-path placeholder fixes.
notes: A small Hyprlayer mark now animates beside the elapsed-time counter while a session is working — a calm, branded progress cue whose three stacked layers glow in a bottom→top wave. It renders static under reduced-motion.

The toolbar terminal button now toggles the terminal: clicking it opens or reveals a hidden terminal and hides a visible one, matching the ⌘` shortcut. The button shows active state and its label switches between “Open terminal” and “Close terminal”; hiding keeps the PTY running for a later reveal.
Fixed misleading placeholder text in the repo path input — it now reads /path/to/your/repo instead of /path/to/your/thoughts.

versions.summary: A broad performance pass: smoother live sessions, GPU terminal, snappier sidebar, faster startup.
notes: Live sessions are noticeably smoother — the transcript and markdown only re-render the one message that is actively streaming (settled messages are memoized), and the text reveal is throttled, so a busy turn no longer bogs down the whole conversation.

The terminal now renders on the GPU via WebGL for fast, crisp output, with the prompt opened at the true grid size so a wrapping line no longer corrupts the redraw; it falls back to the standard renderer automatically if the GPU context is lost. Terminals also open as a login shell, so they pick up your shell profile.

The sidebar stays responsive with many workstreams: git-status checks now run in parallel rather than one after another, and the active worktree refreshes the moment its files change on disk — no window focus required.

Lower background overhead — the PR watcher pauses while the window is unfocused (waking on refocus), and database and filesystem work moved off the UI’s async path, so the app stays responsive during heavy turns.
Faster startup: heavy screens such as the document editor and the terminal/project view now load on demand instead of all up front.

versions.summary: Archive cleanup and worktree pruning, Shift+Tab stage cycling, plus terminal, docs, and Commit fixes.
notes: Workstreams now strip git-ignored build output and dependencies when archived (seeded files like .env are kept), and a new Clean up… button on the Archive page bulk permanent-deletes archives — all of them, or only those older than 30/60/90 days.

Cycle an un-started agent tab through its pipeline stages (General → Research → Plan → Implement → Validate) with a configurable keybinding (default Shift+Tab); the stage locks once the session starts.
Fixed a blank terminal (blinking cursor, no output) when resuming a session after an app restart, caused by reusing a single-use Tauri channel across the attach-then-open path.
Agent-created plans, research, and handoffs written outside the thoughts roots (e.g. under ~/.claude/plans/) now open in the read-only preview instead of failing with “not indexed.”
The manual Commit button now hides while a workstream’s Ship turn is in flight so it can’t race the commit Ship makes itself, and reappears if the ship fails or new uncommitted changes land.
The in-app update check now runs every 3 hours instead of every 6, so new releases surface sooner.

versions.summary: Worktree-copy warning badges, cleaner workstream creation, and self-clearing background tasks.
notes: Projects whose configured worktree-copy files don't resolve against the checkout now show a yellow warning badge on their sidebar row; hover it to see the offending patterns and the suggested fix. The check re-runs on startup, when you change the copy list, and when the window regains focus — so correcting a file on disk and tabbing back clears the warning without a restart.

Creating a workstream now always dismisses the dialog and jumps straight to the new workstream. Seed-copy problems surface on the project's warning badge instead of reopening an empty New workstream prompt.

Background shell tasks no longer linger as a phantom "running" task: reading a task's output file directly — the common case where the agent consumes the output and the completion notification is suppressed — now ends its live tracking.

versions.summary: Shell-style prompt history, configurable per-repo worktree file seeding, and a wider chat area.
notes: Step through the prompts you've already submitted this session with Alt+Up / Alt+Down (remappable in Settings → Keyboard), recalling each one into the composer to edit and resend. A stacked-lines graphic in the agent pane's top-right corner visualizes the history — hover a line to preview a prompt, click to recall — and it's capped at the 15 most recent, current session only.

Configure files that every new worktree should start with: a Worktree Files card in Project Settings writes a copy list to a committable .hyprlayer/settings.toml, and creating a workstream seeds those files (literal paths or globs) from the main checkout into the fresh worktree. Seeding is best-effort — a listed file that's missing is noted, never fatal.
Scrolling up while a reply streams now releases the auto-scroll instead of yanking you back to the bottom, and the view re-locks with a smooth glide once you return to the end.
The chat content area is now wider — 90% of the pane, up from 80% — and switching to a workstream drops the cursor straight into its composer so you can start typing without clicking first.

versions.summary: Compaction summaries fold into a collapsible divider, and finished background tasks now clear themselves.
notes: When a session compacts, the summary the agent writes afterward is now folded into the compaction divider as a collapsible panel — collapsed by default, with a chevron to expand it. Previously that block either flooded the transcript or was hidden entirely; now it sits inline on the divider, the same way a launched skill's body does.

Background shell tasks an agent starts and never checks again — fire-and-forget background commands — now disappear from the composer's background-task indicator as soon as they finish, instead of lingering as a phantom running task. The app acts on the agent's task-completion notification and clears the entry on any terminal status.

versions.summary: Live background shell tasks now surface in the composer toolbar with a status popover.
notes: When an agent leaves background shell tasks running — anything it started with a background Bash command — a pulsing terminal indicator now appears next to the context meter in the composer toolbar. Click it for a popover that lists each task with its label and a live elapsed timer, and click a row to jump the transcript to the call that spawned it.

Workstreams whose turn has finished but still have background shells running now show a distinct violet "background" activity state — on the workstream dot and in the Cmd+P search palette — so you can tell at a glance which sessions still have live processes.

versions.summary: Hyprlayer now runs on Windows (x64), with terminal and project fixes for the platform.
notes: Windows (x64) is now a supported platform: Hyprlayer ships a native Windows installer alongside the macOS (Apple Silicon) build, with the same in-app auto-updates — install it once and future versions arrive through the Update pill.

A set of Windows-specific fixes make agent sessions work end to end: the terminal now closes cleanly when its shell exits, project paths and the default shell (PowerShell) are detected correctly, and the app reliably locates its bundled CLI binary so agents launch as expected.

versions.summary: A guided first-run setup wizard, plus a header breadcrumb alignment fix.
notes: On first launch — or whenever your config is missing — Hyprlayer now opens a three-step setup wizard: enter your name, configure your AI CLI tool inline in an embedded terminal, and connect a thoughts repo by cloning one, picking a folder on disk, or creating a fresh one. You can re-run it anytime from Settings, which also gains an AI tool card showing your CLI's status with one-click reconfigure.

Fixed the header breadcrumb sliding under the window controls when the sidebar collapses — its inset is now derived from the actual left-cluster layout (and the number of visible controls) instead of a hard-coded macOS value, so it aligns correctly on both macOS and Linux.

versions.summary: Keyboard tab cycling, a Content Security Policy, plus terminal, docs, and commit-button fixes.
notes: Cycle through a pane's agent tabs from the keyboard — Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab move forward and back (Ctrl+PageUp / Ctrl+PageDown on Windows and Linux), wrapping at the ends and focusing the agent's composer.
Fixed a freshly opened integrated terminal that could stall at 80×24 — showing the full grid but acting hung — until you reattached; it now fits its pane on open.
Added a Content Security Policy to the desktop app, tightening what the in-app webview is allowed to load.
Commit and Ship buttons now read the live worktree git status, so they stay in lockstep with the Changes panel instead of lingering after you commit from the integrated terminal.
Fixed the attachment picker modal so it sizes correctly instead of overflowing, and long document lists now scroll inside it.
Library and workstream document lookups now match on the sanitized thoughts project key, so docs resolve even when a project's display name differs from its thoughts key.

versions.summary: Integrated terminal, a project board view, and a global Cmd+P search palette.
notes: Open an integrated terminal in the right dock — ⌘` toggles it open, revealed, or hidden. It runs your shell in the workstream's worktree, matches the active theme, remembers its font size (zoom in/out/reset), and keeps the session alive while hidden; shells are torn down only on tab close, workstream archive, or app exit.
Opening a project with no workstream selected now shows a dashboard board — every workstream as a card with its git status and stage — instead of auto-opening the last-used chat.
Press Cmd+P to open a global search palette that fuzzy-matches across all workstreams, live agents, library docs, and worktree files, and jumps straight to whatever you pick.

Docs that an agent writes through a worktree's thoughts/ symlink now resolve to the real file, so opening, saving, revealing, or editing their frontmatter from the library works instead of missing the index.

versions.summary: Archive workspaces non-destructively, OS toasts when agents need attention, and attachment cards for @file.
notes: Archive a workstream from the sidebar to put it on ice without losing the worktree or branch — unarchive or permanently delete it later from the new Archive view.
When an agent transitions to needs-you while the window is unfocused or you're on another tab, a native OS toast fires; clicking it within 15 seconds jumps to that workstream.

Picking a file from the @file dropdown now stages it as an attachment card instead of leaving a raw path in the prompt, and /commands fire on any whitespace-delimited token rather than only at the start of the message.
At 60% context usage a banner suggests running /create_handoff; once the doc is written it attaches as a tab chip and the Eraser button glows amber so Clear & resume picks up where you left off.
Syntax token colors in fenced code blocks now draw from each theme's own palette rather than bleeding Dark+ defaults onto light, claude, cobalt, matrix, and solarized surfaces.

versions.summary: Rewind a conversation to an earlier user message and re-send an edited prompt.
notes: Hover any of your messages in the transcript to reveal a Rewind action that truncates the conversation back to that turn, repopulates the composer with the original prompt for editing, and resumes from the truncated state.
User turns now show a relative timestamp and a copy-prompt button on the same hover toolbar.

versions.summary: Syntax-highlighted code blocks in chat and library markdown.
notes: Fenced code blocks in assistant messages and library docs now render with Shiki syntax highlighting that tracks the active theme.
Highlighting waits for streaming to settle, so messages render plain monospace while they stream and recolor once complete.

versions.summary: Remove project dialog, compact-boundary markers in the transcript, and a stop button that always stops.
notes: Remove a project from the sidebar with a new Remove dialog — optionally delete its directory from disk.
The transcript now shows a labelled divider when a conversation is compacted, so the pause is visible instead of looking like a hang.
The Stop button now hard-kills wedged turns after a short grace window, so a frozen turn can always be stopped.
The Open-in menu now puts your default editor first, and app icons match the surrounding icon weight.
Archiving a workstream whose worktree had become a husk (directory present, .git gone) no longer hangs.

versions.summary: Customizable keyboard shortcuts, per-provider model defaults, and smarter context-doc suggestions.
notes: Set your own keyboard shortcuts for common actions in Settings → Keyboard.
New sessions can default to a chosen model per provider.
Each pane suggests the most relevant context doc (research or plan) for its stage.
The CI Checks panel now flags merge conflicts that block merging.

versions.summary: Live markdown while messages stream, and fixed clipped composer picker dropdowns.
notes: Assistant messages now render markdown live as they stream, instead of showing raw text until the message completes.
The composer mode and model pickers open their dropdowns again — the toolbar overflow fix no longer clips them.

versions.summary: Choose the base branch when creating a workstream.
notes: The New workstream dialog now has a base-branch picker, defaulting to the repo's detected default branch.
Base a workstream off a release line or feature branch instead of always branching from main.

versions.summary: Workstream activity dots, in-place project imports, and split-pane drop and composer toolbar fixes.
notes: Add an existing project from disk in place instead of re-cloning it.
Workstream cards show activity indicator dots while a session is working.
Drag-and-drop now targets the pane under the cursor in a split session.
Composer toolbar collapses to icons on real overflow, never bleeding past the pane edge.

versions.summary: Composer /skill and @file autocomplete, a Commit action, clear-context, and skill-display fixes.
notes: Autocomplete /skills and @files in the composer, with a recognized-skill highlight.
Commit a worktree without shipping, plus push-based PR status sync and check links.
Clear a session to start a fresh conversation, and run more agents concurrently.
Skill activity now shows the skill name and folds its instructions into one row.

versions.summary: Configurable git settings, an Open-in-editor menu, and resizable, responsive layout polish.
notes: Configure branch-name prefix, automerge, archive-on-merge, and delete-branch-on-archive in a redesigned Settings page.
Open the active worktree in any installed editor, terminal, or file manager from the header.
Resizable diff sidebar, a composer that adapts to narrow panes, and toggleable nav icons.

versions.summary: Ship PRs in-app with CI tracking and merge, per-session permission modes, and UI polish.
notes: Ship a workstream to a GitHub pull request from the header, then track CI checks, merge, and archive.
Choose a permission mode per session — Auto, Ask each time, Accept edits, Plan only, or Bypass.
Polished update notifier with release notes, symmetric sidebars, and a primary-button hover fix.

versions.summary: A git source-control panel with staging, rich diffs, and themed file icons.
notes: Stage, unstage, and discard files from a new Changes panel.
Click a change to open a rich unified or side-by-side diff.
Browse the worktree in an All Files tree; scrollbars now match the theme.

versions.summary: File tool calls now show as pin cards with hover-to-preview diffs.
notes: Read/Write/Edit calls render as compact file cards instead of raw paths.
Hover an edit card to preview its line-level diff.

versions.summary: First public build of Hyprlayer with in-app self-update.
notes: Native desktop app for spec-driven development.
Automatic, signed in-app updates on macOS and Windows.
